claims.text: As-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type nanoscale films or nanoribbons have high atomic disorder.
As-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type nanoscale films or nanoribbons have a fine-grained structure.
Atomic disorder is a primary governor of the low-field magnetocaloric response and hysteresis in these films or nanoribbons.
Grain-boundary density is a primary governor of the low-field magnetocaloric response and hysteresis in these films or nanoribbons.
Atomic disorder disrupts long-range magnetic ordering.
Grain boundaries disrupt long-range magnetic ordering.
Atomic disorder and grain boundaries disrupt the cooperative magnetostructural transition responsible for the magnetocaloric effect.
Atomic disorder and grain boundaries broaden or reduce the sharpness of the magnetostructural transition.
Atomic disorder and grain boundaries increase hysteresis.
Moderate post-deposition annealing increases grain size.
Moderate post-deposition annealing reduces atomic disorder.
Annealing-induced reductions in disorder and grain-boundary density restore a sharper magnetostructural transition.
Annealed films or nanoribbons will have a larger magnetocaloric entropy change than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed films or nanoribbons will have lower hysteresis than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealing will move the films or nanoribbons toward bulk-like magnetocaloric behavior.
The magnetocaloric effect in the annealed nanoscale material will remain lower than in bulk material because of geometric constraints.
Heat-transfer limitations will keep the observed effect below bulk behavior.
Heat-transfer rate limits the usable magnetic-cooling cycle frequency.
The hypothesis applies under applied magnetic fields below 1 T near room temperature.
The proposed mechanism is not applicable to bulk samples or equiatomic compositions.
